## Our Focus

::: {.incremental}
- **Design decisions** with years-to-decades timescales
- Infrastructure sizing, land use planning, building codes
- Less emphasis on emergency management or real-time operations
- But the frameworks and tools apply broadly: insurance, humanitarian response, and more
:::

# Theoretical Frameworks

## XLRM Framework

Throughout this course, we'll use the **XLRM Framework** to structure our thinking:

::: {.incremental}
- **X** = e**X**ogenous uncertainties (what we can't control)
- **L** = **L**evers (decisions we can make)
- **R** = **R**elationships (how the system works)
- **M** = **M**etrics (what we care about)
:::

## Other Foundations

We'll also draw on:

::: {.incremental}
- **Economic theory**: utility, welfare, and their limitations
- **Stochastic optimization**: making optimal decisions under uncertainty
- **Deep uncertainty**: what to do when we can't assign probabilities
:::

::: {.fragment}
More on each throughout the semester!
:::

# About the course

## Course goals

Climate risk management is a very broad field.
We will:

1. **Survey** how it is implemented in different fields
1. Develop a **deep understanding** of how to assess proposed climate risk strategies
1. **Apply** these methods to a real-world problem

## Final Project

::: {.callout-important}
## Audit a Real-World Plan

You'll select a climate adaptation or risk management plan and critically evaluate it.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Every climate plan has hidden assumptions
- Every cost-benefit analysis makes value judgments
- You're training to be the experts who **check the work**
- Find the "vibes" hiding in technical documents
:::

## Three modules

1. **Risk Analysis** (Weeks 1-5): Characterize hazards and quantify uncertainty
1. **Decision Analysis** (Weeks 6-9): Evaluate options under uncertainty
1. **Optimization Under Uncertainty** (Weeks 10-13): Find robust strategies

Week 14: Final Project Presentations
